args.body:
MEMORANDUM

TO: Deal Team / Engagement Partners
FROM: Counsel — Energy & Natural Resources Practice
DATE: [Engagement Date]
RE: Redline Review of TxDOT Counterparty Markup of Concession Agreement — Risk Ratings and Counter-Proposal Language

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This memorandum compares the TxDOT counterparty markup of the Concession Agreement (the "Markup") against our original draft (the "Original Draft") and the negotiation playbook, cross-referencing the lender and surety letters and the financial model. The deliverable identifies each deviation introduced by the Markup, assigns a risk rating, and sets forth counter-proposal language for renegotiation. This memorandum is grounded in the operative matter materials and controls in favor of the most recent instruction from the deal team (which revises and supersedes prior statements of priority).

II. GOVERNING PRIORITIES (CONTROLLING INSTRUCTION)

The controlling negotiation instruction directs that the client will (i) concede conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket, but (ii) treat any reduction of the survival period for the core representations as a walk-away issue. Earlier instructions stating a contrary priority ordering are superseded and do not control. Schedules and exhibits referenced in the agreement qualify the general statements in the Original Draft and control where inconsistent.

III. DEVIATIONS IDENTIFIED IN THE TXDOT MARKUP

The Markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations, each reconciled against the Original Draft, the lender and surety letters, and the financial model as follows.

--- DEVIATION 1: INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCTION AND BASKET CONVERSION ---

Original Draft: Indemnification cap at the firm-standard amount, with a deductible basket below which losses are borne by the indemnified party up to a threshold, with the full dollar-for-dollar recovery only above that threshold.

Markup: The indemnification cap is silently reduced, and the basket is converted from a deductible to a tipping basket such that once the threshold is met, the indemnifying party bears all losses from the first dollar.

Cross-Reference — Financial Model: The financial model's exposure and cash-flow assumptions are calibrated to the firm-standard cap. A silent cap reduction is not reflected in the model's risk/pricing margins and would transfer uncompensated risk to the client.

Cross-Reference — Schedules and Lender/Surety Letters: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. The Markup's indemnification changes would silently shift a portion of those retained liabilities (which are backed by the lenders' and sureties' security and recourse expectations) onto the client. This contradicts the lender and surety letter assumptions regarding the allocation of retained obligations and the Credit Support/Surety arrangements.

Risk Rating: HIGH (cap reduction). The cap reduction is a material economic deviation not contemplated by the financial model or the lender/surety allocation, and would transfer significant uncompensated exposure. Per the playbook this is not waived and must be resisted.

Risk Rating: ACCEPT-CONCEDED (basket conversion). Consistent with the controlling instruction, the client will concede conversion from deductible to tipping basket. This is the identified concession item and should be granted only in the form described below.

Counter-Proposal Language (Indemnification Cap):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in Section [•], the aggregate liability of the Concessionaire under the indemnification provisions of this Agreement shall not exceed [•]% of the Total Concession Consideration (the 'Cap'). For the avoidance of doubt, the Cap has not been reduced from the amount set forth in the parties' prior draft, and any purported reduction of the Cap shall be of no force or effect unless expressly agreed in writing by the parties and reflected in an amended financial model."

Counter-Proposal Language (Basket Conversion — Conceded):
"The parties acknowledge that the indemnification basket shall operate as a tipping basket. Once the aggregate amount of losses exceeds the Basket Threshold of $[•], the indemnifying party shall be liable for the full amount of such losses from the first dollar; provided that the Basket Threshold and the Cap set forth herein shall not be reduced and shall remain as set forth in the Original Draft."

--- DEVIATION 2: MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT (MAE) DEFINITION — REGULATORY CARVE-OUTS ---

Original Draft: MAE definition contains the firm-standard carve-outs, which do not include a blanket carve-out for adverse regulatory action, and notably do not exclude the specific type of regulatory findings at issue in this matter.

Markup: The MAE definition is expanded to add carve-outs for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter."

Cross-Reference — Schedules (Schedule 3.7): Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the markup's proposed MAE carve-outs. If the MAE carve-out is accepted as drafted, it would arguably excuse the counterparty (or the concession authority) from the consequences of precisely the regulatory events that have already been disclosed and that the parties had addressed through Schedule 3.7. This would permit the MAE standard to be neutralized by reference to activity the parties knew about at signing, undermining the client's termination and closing protection.

Risk Rating: HIGH. Adding a carve-out for regulatory action of the exact kind at issue would materially weaken the client's MAE protection and render the Schedule 3.7 disclosures effectively moot. This deviation is not supported by the lender or surety letter expectations and is not a conceded item.

Counter-Proposal Language (MAE):
"'Material Adverse Effect' shall not include, and no effect may be deemed a Material Adverse Effect to the extent caused by or arising from: (a) changes in Law, regulation or regulatory policy, or the interpretation or enforcement thereof, except to the extent such change, in the case of regulatory enforcement or inquiry, arises from actions or omissions of the Concessionaire or its Affiliates taken or omitted to be taken in breach of this Agreement or applicable Law; provided that this clause shall not exclude any effect arising from the regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7, which shall remain subject to this Agreement and the conditions to closing set forth herein. For the avoidance of doubt, the carve-out proposed by the Counterparty for regulatory action of the kind disclosed on Schedule 3.7 is rejected."

--- DEVIATION 3: SURVIVAL PERIOD REDUCTION FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS ---

Original Draft: Survival period for the core representations set forth in the survival matrix attached as Exhibit B, with the firm-standard limitation period.

Markup: A new limitation period shortens survival for the core representations.

Cross-Reference — Exhibit B (Survival Matrix): Exhibit B sets the survival matrix. The Markup's shortened limitation period directly contradicts Exhibit B and would reduce the window during which the client may bring claims for breach of the core representations.

Cross-Reference — Negotiation Playbook / Controlling Instruction: Per the governing instruction, any survival-period reduction for the core representations is a WALK-AWAY ISSUE. This is the highest-priority red line and must not be conceded.

Risk Rating: CRITICAL / WALK-AWAY. Reduction of the survival period for the core representations contradicts Exhibit B and the controlling instruction. This is a walk-away issue; the client should not accept any reduction of the firm-standard survival period for the core representations.

Counter-Proposal Language (Survival):
"The representations and warranties of the parties set forth in Article III (and, for the counterparty, in the corresponding representation sections) shall survive the Closing for the periods set forth in the survival matrix attached as Exhibit B, and no provision of this Agreement shall be construed to shorten such survival periods. The parties expressly reject any new limitation period that would reduce the survival of the core representations below the periods set forth in Exhibit B, and recede from the Counterparty's proposed shortening in the Markup."

IV. CROSS-REFERENCE SUMMARY TABLE

| Deviation | Original Draft Position | TxDOT Markup Position | Cross-Reference | Risk Rating | Recommended Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1a. Indemnification Cap | Firm-standard cap | Silently reduced | Financial model; Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities; lender/surety letters | HIGH | Reject / Counter — restore firm-standard cap |
| 1b. Basket | Deductible basket | Tipping basket | Playbook (conceded) | ACCEPT-CONCEDED | Concede per controlling instruction |
| 2. MAE carve-outs | No carve-out for the regulatory action at issue | Carve-out for precisely that regulatory action | Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries) | HIGH | Reject / Counter — delete carve-out |
| 3. Survival Period | Per Exhibit B survival matrix | Shortened limitation period | Exhibit B; playbook (walk-away) | CRITICAL / WALK-AWAY | Reject — do not concede; walk-away if maintained |

V. RECOMMENDED NEGOTIATION STRATEGY

Track the three deviations against the conceded basket conversion, the resisted cap and MAE deviations, and the non-negotiable survival period:

1. Concede the basket conversion (Deviation 1b) as the primary concession, in the form set forth above, in exchange for the counterparty's agreement to restore the firm-standard cap (Deviation 1a) and delete the MAE carve-out (Deviation 2).
2. Hold firm on the survival period (Deviation 3), which is a walk-away issue. Any indication by the counterparty that survival of the core representations will be shortened should trigger escalation to the partner and consideration of the walk-away threshold.
3. Ensure the final executed agreement is reconciled against Exhibit B and Schedule 3.7, and that no silent cap reduction or basket conversion beyond the conceded form finds its way into the operative text.

VI. MARKUP-LEVEL RECOMMENDATION

The Markup should be returned to TxDOT together with the full redline incorporating the counter-proposal language in Section III above. The client concedes the basket conversion. The cap reduction and the MAE regulatory carve-out are rejected with supporting rationale grounded in the financial model, Schedule 3.7 and the lender/surety expectations. The survival-period reduction is a non-negotiable walk-away matter and must not be accepted under any circumstances.

Prepared by: Associate (Energy & Natural Resources)
Reviewed by: Partner
